# [PR #413] fix: randomize float inputs each iteration to prevent output caching

source: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer-bench/pull/413
state: open | updated: 2026-04-23T13:14:58Z
labels: 

## 正文

Fixes #228

## Problem

Kernels can cheat the benchmark by caching outputs keyed on input `data_ptr()` during warmup, then returning cached results in timed iterations. The PoC in #228 demonstrates ~12.90x apparent speedup with zero actual computation.

## Fix

Wrap `fn` in `_fn_with_randomized_inputs` which calls `uniform_()` on all floating-point input tensors before each iteration, breaking any pointer-based or value-based output cache.

Integer/index tensors (e.g. `kv_indptr`, `kv_indices`) are intentionally left unchanged to preserve structural validity of attention metadata.

### gemini-code-assist[bot] · 2026-04-23 · COMMENTED

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a mechanism to randomize floating-point input tensors in-place before each benchmark iteration to prevent output caching. However, the review identifies critical issues: the randomization overhead is currently included in the measured execution time, and since the operation is in-place, it does not change memory pointers, which may fail to bypass pointer-based caching. Additionally, the current logic does not handle nested tensor containers, and there is an unnecessary list allocation in the wrapper function.

> `81-95`: _⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_
> 
> **Randomization kernel time is included in the measured latency.**
> 
> `arg.uniform_()` launches a CUDA kernel per floating-point tensor on the same stream as `fn`. `bench_gpu_time_with_cupti` measures GPU kernel activity during each invocation of the wrapped callable, so the time of these `uniform_()` kernels is added to every timed iteration. This inflates `sol_latencies` and directly distorts `speedup_factor` computed in `flashinfer_bench/bench/evaluators/default.py` (line 220) — the fix trades one measurement error (caching) for another (timing overhead that scales with input tensor sizes and count).
> 
> Additionally, in DPS style the output tensor(s) (allocated in `allocate_outputs`) are appended to the input args before timing, so they are also randomized—unnecessary extra work that contributes to timing inflation.
> 
> Consider randomizing inputs outside the timed region. For example, pre-generate N randomized input sets and let the benchmark cycle through them, or modify the underlying benchmarker to support a `pre_iter` hook excluded from timing. At minimum, quantify the overhead of `uniform_()` relative to the kernels being benchmarked and document this trade-off explicitly.

`_randomize_float_inputs` only iterates; a tuple works directly. Also, using a seeded `torch.Generator` (per device) would keep iteration-to-iteration inputs varying while making runs reproducible across processes, which is useful for debugging timing regressions.
